title: Michael James David Powell. 29 July 1936 — 19 April 2015 (Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society)
contribution: Full-length biographical memoir (DAMTP NA2017/04 preprint of the Royal Society memoir) that documents Powell's career 1936–2015, frames him as refusing the designer/theoretician split, and supplies dates, named doctoral students, working habits and a list of 83 Powell papers; the DFO era gets only one paragraph (p. 17).
problem_entry: Memoir opens with a thesis sentence (Powell refused the theory/practice dichotomy, p. 3); it shows Powell entering problems through Harwell's code-for-others remit and industrial DFO demand (pp. 5–6), a hard-to-read report (Davidon, p. 6), gaps observed in practice (DFP vs BFGS, p. 9), celebrated results to test (Karmarkar, p. 17) and practitioner contact (p. 17).
key_idea: Keep a working framework and change one lever: shift of origin instead of growing penalty (augmented Lagrangian, p. 7), variable metric applied to constrained optimality conditions (SQP, p. 14), ratio-controlled trust region (p. 19), cheap models of expensive functions — RBF tried and dropped, then polynomial interpolation (p. 17); positive-definiteness preserved via partial updating (p. 15).
assumptions: Memoir rests on the authors' recollections, the Davis 2005 and Vicente 2003 interviews and one non-Powell paper (p. 26); priority claims asserted without external citations (pp. 15, 19); several bracket citations mismatched (pp. 6, 8, 14, 15, 19 vs list pp. 27–28); reports Powell's DFO premise of expensive user-supplied functions with cheap model work (p. 17).
proof_devices: counterexamples to widely held beliefs: coordinate search non-convergence (p. 8), cycling in a feasible point algorithm [28] (p. 16), Karmarkar complexity example (p. 17)
smallest-case analysis: two-variable quadratic with inexact line search explaining DFP worse than BFGS (p. 9)
negative-result theorem: CG cannot converge superlinearly without periodic steepest-descent restarts (p. 8)
proof-enabling safeguards: dog-leg trajectory enabling a Gauss–Newton convergence proof (p. 6); actual/predicted reduction ratio for radius updates aimed at global convergence (p. 19)
first convergence proof for DFP with exact line search (p. 9); SQP convergence theory (p. 14); trust-region global convergence series 1984–2015 (p. 15)
counting conditions against degrees of freedom (Powell–Sabin split, nine conditions, p. 20)
removing a domain-regularity (Lipschitz boundary) assumption while keeping the best rate up to log h, plus best constants on 2-, 3-, 4-point configurations (thin-plate splines, p. 23)
dynamic programming with recursive data reduction (p. 19); RBF interpolation-matrix nonsingularity (p. 21)
experiments: none in the memoir; reports Powell's practice: 100-variable DFP demonstrations (p. 7), early DFO beaten by finite-difference gradient methods (p. 8), RBF models dropped after numerical tests (pp. 17, 21), DFP–BFGS gap observed in practice before analysis (p. 9).
positioning: Powell credits predecessors and states his added value (SQP after Han and Biggs: clarification, implementation, convergence theory, p. 14; DFP from Davidon's report, pp. 6–7) and critiques rivals by constructed example (pp. 8, 17); memoir concedes his theoretical interest decreased in the DFO years (p. 17).
writing: Memoir is chronological, laudatory and low in hedging (p. 14), interleaving interview quotes (pp. 10–12); it reports Powell's style: more explanations and fewer formulae (p. 18), two-page handwritten lecture notes (p. 12), colour-coded slides (p. 18), surveys that improve proofs (p. 22), quality-and-relevance editing (p. 12).
limits_future: DFO era covered in one paragraph (p. 17); COBYLA, BOBYQA, LINCOA never named and BOBYQA/LINCOA absent from the reference list (pp. 32–33); retirement-era software unidentified (p. 24); mismatched bracket citations; admitted limits of Powell's work: partial updating loses curvature (p. 15), restarts ineffective for very large problems (p. 9), RBF models failed in optimization (p. 17); no future directions.

method_links.note: Free dissemination of reports and software decades before funders required it; Harwell remit to write subroutines for others; code-as-report practice from 1970 (Harwell Fortran subroutine reports [9], [12]) and 1982–1989 (VMCWD, ZQPCVX, TOLMIN) predates COBYLA; finished software before death.
RBF models for optimization dropped after numerical tests; large-n DFP demonstrations; practice-observed gaps (DFP vs BFGS) precede theory.
DFO papers progress unconstrained → bound-constrained → linearly constrained with a continuously improving view of second-order model information.

Relax-one-limitation also at programme and theorem level: SQP transplants variable metric to constraints; sparse Jacobian estimate extended to symmetric Hessians; thin-plate-spline convergence without Lipschitz boundary at the same rate.

DFO premise of cheap model work vs expensive evaluations; 2011 lecture on a parsimonious way of constructing quadratic models; least-change heritage in quasi-Newton low-rank updates and PSB; Powell's own 2013 title 'Beyond symmetric Broyden' (title only) bears on Method 3's unverified 'other norms' limitation.
Partial: memoir credits Powell with pioneering trust regions (1970) and introducing the actual/predicted ratio test for the radius (DELTA half); silent on RHO.

Weak, from approximation theory: truncated Laurent expansions to minimize costly logarithm evaluations; interest in efficient and accurate computation and implementation; QP solvers treated as necessary for robust SQP codes.
The 'refused to follow this dichotomy' characterization, held in SKILL.md only as a snippet paraphrase, is verified as an actual memoir sentence.

Memoir confirms theory interest decreased in DFO years, but Powell himself published DFO trust-region convergence papers ([73] 2003, [81] 2012; contents not read), so 'shipped without guarantees' should be limited to complexity guarantees.

SKILL.md says doctoral students are unverified; memoir names Toint, Yuan, Gutmann (PhD) and Demetriou (research student). Dates: Harwell 1959–76, Plummer Chair 1976, retired 2001; augmented Lagrangian late 1960s at Harwell; SQP after 1976; RBF models were the abandoned path before polynomial-interpolation DFO.

transferable: To explain why method A beats method B in practice, build the smallest instance (two variables, quadratic, one specific inexact line search) where the gap appears and analyse it exactly (p. 9).
Challenge a celebrated convergence or complexity claim with an explicit violating instance rather than general argument (pp. 8, 17).
When a global convergence proof fails, modify the step (dog-leg path, ratio-controlled radius) so that the proof goes through, and keep the safeguard in the code (pp. 6, 19).
If a method reaches the answer only as a penalty parameter goes to infinity, look for an additive shift of origin that reaches it at a finite value and identify the shift with multipliers (p. 7).
Present a new method as a proven mechanism applied to a new problem class (SQP as variable metric for constrained optimization) so readers inherit the intuition and local-rate expectations (p. 14).
Fix the structural invariant the model must keep (positive definiteness); when data would break it, update partially and state what information is lost (p. 15).
Test a candidate model class inside the optimization loop before investing in it; drop it for that use if tests disappoint (RBF, pp. 17, 21).
When improving a theorem, target one regularity assumption and show the rate survives its removal; then compute best constants on the smallest configurations (p. 23).
Count continuity conditions against degrees of freedom before choosing a piecewise split (Powell–Sabin, p. 20).
When building on another's idea, name the originators and state your contribution as clarification, implementation and convergence theory (p. 14).
Write surveys that re-prove the covered results more simply or sharply (pp. 18, 22).
coauthors: M. D. Buhmann, R. Fletcher, A. Iserles, P. Toint (memoir authors; Powell is the subject)

quotes.text: In a subject that roughly divides into practical designers of algorithms and theoreticians who seek to underpin algorithms with solid mathematical foundations, Mike Powell refused to follow this dichotomy.
it displays Mike’s remarkable talent for producing intriguing counter-examples to sometimes widely held beliefs
